findings.failure_mode: missing file, permission denied, or disk full aborts the entire request instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or explicit map_err

findings.problem: splits on ',' then collects all parts into Vec<String> then indexes by position; skill mandates split_once when only one delimiter extraction is needed
findings.failure_mode: allocates a Vec of Strings for every line, then indexes with unchecked indexing — both allocation and bounds-unsafe
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get (name, value) directly, then trim and parse each half

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked array indexing — no bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: an empty line or line with zero commas causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') which returns Option<(>&str, &str)> and handle None via map_err or early return

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", ...) is a side effect inside a data-loading function that should be pure
findings.failure_mode: core logic leaks logging into what should be a deterministic calculation; breaks testability and purity of the functional core
findings.fix: remove println! from the core; logging belongs in the imperative shell at the boundary where the result is consumed

findings.problem: parts[1] is unchecked array indexing — no bounds check before access
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one comma-separated field causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on the Option<(name, value)> tuple instead of indexing

findings.failure_mode: malformed invoice data (e.g. non-numeric value field) aborts the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ... ) and propagate the error through a Result return type

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width-cast from u32 — values > 65535 silently wrap
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 stored as u16 becomes 4465 without any error, corrupting invoice data silently
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value) and handle TryFromIntError with map_err, or parse directly as u16 if domain guarantees fit

findings.problem: load_invoices mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with data parsing and transformation — should be split into pure parse function and imperative shell caller
findings.failure_mode: the core transformation logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation; every test requires file-system access
findings.fix: extract a pure fn parse_invoice(line: &str) -> Result<Record, InvoiceError> and have load_invoices call it with map_err

findings.problem: Record struct uses pub fields with String — allows mutation from any caller, violating immutability of domain data by construction
findings.failure_mode: any crate consumer can mutate name or value after construction, breaking the invariant that parsed records are immutable
findings.fix: make Record fields private with a constructor fn new(name: String, value: u16) -> Self, or use #[derive(Accessor)] pattern

no second-ring evidence: no Miri run, no Kani harness, no property tests for invoice parsing invariants

residual_risk: static review only; multiple BLOCKER violations including unwrap panics, unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden logging, and no functional-core separation. The crate cannot be safely deployed — every line of the parse path can panic or silently corrupt data on malformed input.
